implication: Regulation 31(4) is a gating disclosure for any person intending to acquire shares that would trigger the 25% (or other threshold) under Regulation 4; practitioners must confirm the threshold triggering the filing, the timeline to complete acquisition, and whether post-acquisition open offer obligations under Regulation 4 apply.

framework.note: Defines substantial acquisition thresholds (25%, 35%, 48%, 55%, 65%, 75%) and triggers mandatory open offer requirement.
Pre-acquisition disclosure requirement: acquirer must notify exchange of intent to acquire before crossing thresholds.
Acquirer must seek CCI approval (if applicable under Competition Act) before acquisition.
Post-acquisition disclosure: within 4 trading days of acquiring shares crossing a threshold, disclosure to exchange required.
Combinations notifiable to CCI if relevant financial thresholds met (₹2,000 cr asset turnover in India or ₹6,000 cr global).

headline: Bimal Lalitsingh Goculdas files substantial acquisition disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Bimal Lalitsingh Goculdas has submitted a Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE, signalling an intended or recent substantial shareholding in DMCC Speciality Chemicals Limited. The filing is a mandatory pre-acquisition or post-acquisition transparency requirement under SEBI's takeover regime.
detail: Under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations 2011, Regulation 31(4) requires disclosure to the exchange of an intent to acquire or recent acquisition of substantial shareholding before the acquisition is executed (or immediately after, if already executed). The filing by Bimal Lalitsingh Goculdas to NSE indicates either an imminent acquisition or a post-facto declaration of a recent holding change. The disclosure document submitted to NSE archives contains the detailed shareholding position, PAC (persons acting in concert), and timeline.
